title: Prefetch compact kernel index & deferred symbolization to cut cold-start latency
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background:
Cold-start latency during container warmup is contributing ~120-250ms additional p95 for first requests on freshly started GPU workers. Investigation shows the runtime currently probes a large set of provider shared objects and performs eager symbol resolution which triggers heavy IO and linker activity on nodes with many optional kernel variants.

Goal:
- Reduce cold-start p95 by 40-60% for newly provisioned GPUs without changing runtime ABI.
- Maintain deterministic fallback behavior and keep on-disk artifacts unchanged for compatibility.

Proposal (high level):
1) Introduce a compact kernel index artifact (JSONL) generated at packaging time that enumerates available kernel variants and their minimal probe hints (soname, version tag, required symbol set). This file is <100KB for typical bundles and will be memory-mapped at startup.
2) Implement a lightweight provider shim that uses the compact index to perform targeted prefetch of at most N shared objects (configurable) instead of scanning the full provider graph. The shim will also record a cold-start telemetry sample for each node.
3) Defer full symbolization (dlopen/dlsym) for non-critical kernels: use a two-tier lookup where symbol resolution happens on first use with a bounded timeout; meanwhile, early requests may fall back to a safe CPU/compat path or a quantized variant.
4) Add an opt-in feature gate and config flags for aggressive prefetching vs. conservative probe behavior. Default to conservative on Dedicated and Private deployments until we validate.

Implementation steps:
- Packager: add kernel-index-generator to build pipeline; include schema version and checksum. (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/pkg-tools/pull/572)
- Runtime: add provider_shim.{cc,hh} with a modular prefetch strategy and mmap loader for index. Feature flag runtime.prefetch.index
- Telemetry: add cold_start.sample_count + prefetch_hit_ratio to statsd and console. Dashboard: /dashboards/runtime/cold-start
- Tests: unit tests for index parsing, emulator tests for selective dlopen, integration canaries on canary pool with slow-storage simulation.

Trade-offs and risks:
- Slightly more complexity in packaging and an extra artifact to manage across releases. Mitigation: auto-generate index in CI and include version checks.
- Deferred symbolization might surface latent missing-symbol regressions only at first-use; mitigate by enhanced CI canaries that exercise critical kernels and by enabling a preflight check in Dedicated+Private releases.

Rollout plan:
- Stage 1 (canary): runtime-1.23-alpha with index generation enabled in CI; deploy to 5% canary pool; collect telemetry for 1 week.
- Stage 2 (gradual): increase to 25% with conservative prefetch; run perf/eval suites, monitor fallback rate.
- Stage 3: enable on all hosted with defaults; enable opt-in aggressive behavior for Dedicated customers via config.

Acceptance criteria:
- Cold-start p95 reduced by >=40% on canary clusters in simulated cold-start tests.
- Prefetch_hit_ratio > 0.75 and fallback_rate < 1% for default settings.
- No increase in steady-state latency or request error rate.

2025-02-25: PR opened for packager: github.com/redwood-inference/pkg-tools/pull/572 — awaiting CI. Added unit tests for schema v1 parsing. — Asha Patel

2025-03-01: Runtime shim initial commit posted: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1918. Needs integration tests for dlopen fallback timeout path. Spike shows prefetch_hit_ratio ~0.82 with N=3. — Marcus Nguyen

2025-03-04: QA flagged potential race during deferred symbolization when two threads attempt symbol resolve concurrently; added a singleflight guard in shim. Rescheduled integration testing. — Priya Sinha (QA)
